<objective>
Make Fleet's requirement trackers tell the truth about what Phase 2 actually shipped, and repair the ROADMAP
Progress table that silently lost a phase.

Purpose: `02-VERIFICATION.md` independently re-verified fourteen requirement IDs as genuinely implemented
and tested, and found the tracking documents disagreeing about them. The disagreement is not uniform, which
is what makes it worth a task rather than a one-line edit: REQUIREMENTS.md carries TWO independent trackers
for the same facts — a checkbox list per section and a Phase Tracking table at the bottom — and for these
fourteen IDs the checkbox list is already correct while the Phase Tracking table still reads `Pending`. The
verification report describes both as stale; the file itself shows otherwise. Reconciling against the file
rather than against the report is the whole job.

This is a documentation task with a hard boundary: it records what has been proven, and it must not become
the mechanism by which an unproven thing acquires a tick. Three ID groups are explicitly out of its reach.

Output: two trackers that agree with each other and with the code, each entry carrying an evidence pointer;
a ROADMAP Progress table that matches the phase list it summarises; and a confirmation that the phase's API
coverage artifact is present and well-formed.
</objective>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| a plan's self-reported `requirements-completed` -> a project-level tracker | A claim crossing into a document later readers treat as fact, without a re-verification hop between |
| a deliberate deferral -> a batch update | A group intentionally held back being swept complete because it resembles the batch around it |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-2-47 | Repudiation | requirement trackers updated from claims rather than evidence | high | mitigate | Task 1 mandates a per-ID re-read of the implementing module or test before any tick, names `02-06-SUMMARY.md`'s overstated RUN-06 claim as the concrete precedent, and requires a per-ID evidence clause in the file so the claim is re-checkable rather than merely asserted |
| T-2-48 | Tampering | a deliberate deferral silently converted to complete | high | mitigate | The AGENT-01…06 group and TASK-05/RUN-06 are excluded by explicit acceptance criteria that assert their rows still read pending after the task runs — an over-eager batch edit fails the task rather than passing quietly |
| T-2-49 | Repudiation | the phase's Mode-tag mismatch erased instead of escalated | medium | mitigate | Task 2 forbids editing the Mode tag or Goal line, asserts both are byte-identical afterwards, and requires the outstanding human decision to be recorded in the summary |
| T-2-50 | Information Disclosure | a malformed coverage matrix passing the seal gate | medium | mitigate | Task 2's automated verify asserts no opt-out row carries an empty reason cell, which is the specific malformation the gate exists to catch |
| T-2-51 | Spoofing | a documentation-only plan being used to close a functional gap | low | accept | Single-user project; the acceptance criteria pin the excluded IDs positively, and the functional gaps are closed by plans that ship code and tests. No further control is warranted at ASVS L1 |
</threat_model>
